title: Install a drip emitter: punch the 1/2 in drip line square at the mark, then push the barbed dripper in until it seats
instruction: Install the dripper in the drip line at the white mark, then put the punch back in its block.
context: Landscaping and groundskeeping workers (O*NET 37-3011, about 1.0M US workers) install and maintain irrigation systems as part of their listed tasks; on drip systems, adding a dripper for a new plant or replacing a clogged one is done the same way every time, dozens per bed: punch a hole in the 1/2 in poly line with an emitter punch, then push the dripper's barb into it until it pops in to its collar. The punch must go through the wall on the mark, square to the round tube, with about 25 N: angled, it slips and tears a slit that leaks. The barb must then find the 3 mm hole, hidden under the dripper's 30 mm body, and be pushed in square with about 15 N; crooked, it tears the hole. A second hole leaks too.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, on the table top (x forward, y left). Bed: 12 mm plywood 30 x 64 cm under brown landscape fabric, centred x 33, y -2. Drip line: 1/2 in poly drip tubing (0.700 in / 17.8 mm OD, ~0.9 mm wall), 62 cm, lying along y at x 30 from y -33 to +29, ends closed with figure-8 end closures, held by two Rain Bird TS-025 wire tubing stakes at y -20.5 and +4.5. Mark: white paint-pen ring 3 mm wide round the tube at y -8 (seeded -9.5 to -6.5). Shrub: artificial boxwood ~14 cm across in a black 1 gal nursery pot (16.5 cm across, 17 cm tall) at x 45, y -8, just behind the mark. Tool block: pine 2x4 offcut 89 x 120 x 38 mm, flat on the bed centred x 40, y -25, long side along y, with a 6 mm hole at y -28.8 and a 5 mm hole at y -21.2, 34 mm deep (drawing in README). Emitter punch (Netafim 682901033, 3 mm point, yellow plastic handle ~28 mm across x 87 mm, 40 g) standing point down in the 6 mm hole, its stop shoulder on the block. Barbed dripper (Netafim Woodpecker PC with barbed base, 30 mm across, 21 mm tall above a 4 x 7 mm barb, 2 g) standing barb down in the 5 mm hole. Nothing else on the table; arms in the ready pose.
scoring: Scored at the end from the line, the punch and the video. 0.4: a round hole punched within 10 mm of the white mark along the line (ruler; close photo: round, no slit or tear over 4 mm). +0.5: the dripper seated in that hole (photo: its base touches the tube all round; it does not come off with a firm hand pull). +0.1: then the punch standing back in its block hole, point down, released (photo). A torn hole (punched more than 15 deg off square, or the dripper forced in more than 15 deg off square; real trial: a slit over 4 mm once the dripper is pulled out) or a second hole anywhere on the line caps the score at 0.2. Success: 1.0 held 1 s.
reset_notes: Pull the dripper out; slide the tube along the stakes to an unpunched stretch (or fit a fresh 62 cm length), draw a new white ring, stand the punch and a new dripper in their block holes. A punched stretch and the dripper are used up (about 3 cm of tube and $0.40 per trial).
fidelity: Approximate. Rigid bodies; the staked line is fixed. A rule stands in for the wall: a hole appears at the punch's point once it has pushed on the tube with 25 N (+-10% per seed) for 0.1 s; torn if over 15 deg off the surface normal. The dripper seats once its barb tip is within 1.5 mm of a hole and it pushes 15 N for 0.1 s within 15 deg of square (then held seated); crooked, it tears the hole. Forces are estimates (README: how to measure them). Dripper 20 g in the solver.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (seed 0, 2,000 steps, step limit; never grasped the punch); scripted demo: 1.0 (seeds 0, 4 and 10, 830-960 steps); contrasts: no punch 0.0, light push 0.0, second hole 0.2
